clip.note: Global 6.40–7.45s. The source is the inspiration; the native V05 blur is a rejected implementation.

inspiration.purpose: Transfer attention from outgoing product assets to a clearer incoming phrase without a blank reset.
beats: Outgoing cards and heading become softer while still visible.
Their composition retreats; opacity falls on its own curve.
Endless arrives larger, lower and farther left, then reduces with a long tail.
Confirmation rises into the same changing framing while old assets finish leaving.
use_when: The next reading target can gain clarity before the previous group disappears.
Depth retreat and focus can reinforce a continuous handoff.
inspiration.attention: Old assets lose clarity and prominence as the new words become readable.

meta.label: Independent controls
meta.value: Retreat, defocus, opacity and incoming word motion

meta.label: Blur distinction
meta.value: Apparent defocus; distinguish composite blur, temporal motion blur and physical depth of field when reconstructing it

technical.basis: The visible rectangular clipping is established by the comparison. Its exact live effect-setting cause and the proposed repair remain unverified.

sections.title: Separate the control curves
items: Outgoing scale/position, Gaussian softness and opacity have distinct endpoints. Incoming copy has its own arrival and shared framing curve.
The native asset pass already contains depth retreat; the AE focus effect adds softness rather than a second retreat.

sections.title: Observed failure
items: At global 6.70s the heading and individual subtitle words show hard rectangular blur boundaries. The reference softness extends beyond glyph bounds.
Increasing blur strength preserves the clipping and can make it more obvious. V05 values below document the rejected candidate; they are not recommended defaults.

sections.title: Prepared correction — not rendered
items: V06 proposes auditing and disabling Gaussian Repeat Edge Pixels, then rendering six check frames. If clipping persists, use a padded full-frame text precomposition and apply defocus after it.
Keep V05 movement and opacity fixed for the boundary test. Inspect6.55,6.70,6.85,6.95,7.20 and 8.15s before rerendering the passage.
The visible boundary fault does not prove that Repeat Edge Pixels is the culprit. Do not mark this fix as successful before inspecting the new output.

sections.title: Acceptance
items: Softness extends beyond letters without rectangles at all visible radii and scales. Focus loss is visible before opacity removes the group.
Incoming copy remains the clear reading target and old assets finish leaving. Check full playback as well as the maximum-blur frame.

parameters.name: V06 edge-control test
parameters.value: Disable repeated edges; padded precomp fallback

implementations.label: V05 rejected blur, retained for comparison

review.inspection: Dense reference and encoded frame samples; no new continuous playback or audio review is claimed by this library integration.
review.scope: V05 outgoing blur rejected for visible rectangular clipping. V06 has not been rendered; no repaired blur is approved.
limitations: Blur-boundary root cause remains unverified in the live project.
No V06 render or native success claim.
